gap: No result ChatGPT got states how long a drained kit takes to refill from its own panel, or how many days the battery can carry the camera with no sun. Worked out from the makers' own figures: a fully drained eufyCam S3 Pro needs about 16–52 days of optimal sun to refill (13,000 mAh at a net 250–800 mAh per day). A drained Reolink Argus PT Ultra needs about 22 days of eufy-style 'claimed minimum' sun (21.6 Wh at 1 Wh per day from 20 minutes on its 3 W panel). So the battery reserve (about 60–130 days) is what gets these cameras through winter, not the panel's wattage.
standout_why: Compared against the cited Bob Vila, SafeWise, HomeGearLab and RottenWiFi pages, the other ranked HomeGearLab page, and the cited solargenadvisor page, which would not load (TLS certificate error). Bob Vila gives mAh for some picks but no panel watts and no ratio. SafeWise gives mAh and two panel ratings (3.2 W, about 2.5 W) but says outright that it can't convert to Wh and computes nothing. HomeGearLab copies eufy's 450–900 mAh gain against 100–200 mAh use for the S3 Pro and Tapo's minutes of sun, but never turns them into days of reserve or days to refill. RottenWiFi lists 5,000 mAh and 6 W for the Argus 4 Pro with no derived figure. None of these pages puts the candidates into one comparable unit.
decides: This backs the eufyCam S3 Pro kit for shady or northern sites: its own figures give at least 2.25× surplus on a sunny day (450 ÷ 200) and 65–130 days on battery alone. It counts against the Reolink Argus 4 Pro for those sites. Its maker claims only about 2 months per charge at 300 s of recording a day, about half the 4 months Reolink claims for the 21.6 Wh Eco Ultra and PT Ultra. For the shopper who 'just needs a panel', it shows that a bigger panel shortens refills but does not add reserve days. Reserve is the battery's job.
